Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Parse CSV Contents
nodes.notes: Parses the incoming CSV binary into JSON items.

nodes.name: Clean & Reshape Rows
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Normalize incoming document records to a stable schema Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Rows Pass Validation?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.documentId }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

nodes.name: Quarantine Bad Rows
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'tracking sheet' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Load Rows into Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Document Tracker', matched on documentId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Load Previous Snapshot
nodes.notes: Pulls every page from the Notion database — fine for small datasets; add a filter if the database grows large. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.name: Compute Drift vs Snapshot
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Compare current metrics with the previous snapshot Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Fold In Enrichment Fields
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes enrichedAt, enrichmentSource. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per document (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Serialize Run Output (CSV)
nodes.notes: Serializes items to a CSV binary file.

nodes.name: Archive Row Snapshot
nodes.notes: Creates a new page in the Notion database — the title is pulled straight from the item's key field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. # Generate contracts with HTTP / REST API and Google Sheets for your team

**Pattern:** Document Generation · **Level:** Architect · **Trigger:** Webhook

## What it does
Generate contracts with HTTP / REST API and Google Sheets for your team. It fires the moment an external system calls its webhook.

## Why it exists
Manual ocr & extraction is slow and error-prone; this workflow makes the process repeatable, monitored and hands-off, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow
Receive Inbound Webhook → Download Source File → Parse CSV Contents → Clean & Reshape Rows → Rows Pass Validation? → Load Rows into Google Sheets → Load Previous Snapshot → …

## Use it for
- Teams that want to document generation without manual effort
- Anyone automating ocr & extraction in legal
- Replacing a fragile manual process with a reliable workflow

## You get
- Runs 24/7 in the background
- Scales without extra headcount
- Standardizes the process every time

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account; Notion integration token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Bad rows are quarantined into their own store, not dropped silently and not allowed to break the whole batch — one malformed row in a 10,000-row file shouldn't stop the other 9,999 from loading, but it also shouldn't vanish without a trace.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Feed it a file with a few deliberately malformed rows and confirm they land in quarantine, not the main store.
2. Switch the source format (e.g. csv to xlsx) and see how little actually has to change.
3. Turn on archive mode and confirm the processed file gets repacked and stored.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).
_Gotcha:_ Add n8n's OAuth redirect URL exactly as shown in the credential, or the consent loop fails.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🔐 Security

Never trust inbound payloads: the webhook path is unguessable. Add header auth or IP allow-listing for defense in depth. Secrets live in n8n credentials — never in node parameters.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your ocr & extraction process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
